editorial_notes: All82 actual units received an initial curated pass, with at least one retained pair per unit. No fixed number of matches was imposed; completion is not exhaustive discovery. All intrachapter connections carry the Same-chapter prefix.
The source's chapter7 has29 units and ends with the frog warning. Its7:26-29 are not silently relocated to another edition's chapter8; the frog outbreak begins in this edition's8:1-2.

The king's idleness accusation and explanation of the worship request remain his speech, distinct from the narrator's painful labour, unchanged quota, stubble-gathering and scourging notices. Different population-policy speeches do not establish the identity or reign of an unnamed Pharaoh.

The labour roles remain taskmasters and scribes as supplied; the text's Israelite scribes, their petitions, Pharaoh's response, their accusation of Moses/Aaron and Moses' appeal to God are kept as different narrative and speech levels.

Straw not being supplied is not made a claim that no material exists anywhere; the people gather stubble. Pharaoh's unchanged count is compared with its actual enforcement without introducing a new modern production estimate.
The release promises are not made completed events before the departure narration. The later frog-period royal promise is not treated as a completed departure either.

Exodus6:3 says appearing as their God, and Genesis17:1 says I am your God. No Almighty title is imported. The name-Lord disclosure statements remain supplied, without a new harmonization of every earlier name occurrence.
Exodus6:5 retains your covenant, alongside the earlier narrator's His covenant in2:24 and the psalm's ancestral-covenant summary. These are not silently turned into one identical quotation.
Exodus29:45-46 says called upon among Israel, and Leviticus26:11 says covenant among them. The chosen links do not replace those supplied forms with dwelling/tabernacle wording from another edition.

Exodus6:9 expressly explains the failure to listen by discouragement and hard labour, not by Pharaoh's charge of idleness or an invented universal spiritual diagnosis. Moses' subsequent inference about Pharaoh remains his own argument.

The source lifespans remain Levi137, Kohath130 and Amram132. Jochebed is the daughter of Amram's father's brother here; Numbers26:59 retains its own difficult daughter-of-Levi and Egypt-birth wording. No aunt-for-cousin substitution or reconstructed ancestry is imposed.

Simeon's six sons and Phoenician mother differ from Genesis' supplied names/Canaanite description and Numbers' five clan headings. Chronicles' Gedson/Lobeni/Semei, Kaath/Ambram/Issaar/Oziel and Mooli/Omousi remain its supplied forms, not silent corrections of Exodus.

Exodus6:22 Elzaphan/Sithri is compared with Numbers' Elizaphan and Leviticus' Misadai/Elzaphan, without treating the differently named additional sons as resolved identities. Elisheba's relationship to Amminadab and Nahshon does not transfer her brother's Judah-representative office to her.

Exodus6:24 lists Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph as Korah's sons; Chronicles6:7-8 uses a descent chain including Kore, Asir, Elkanah and Abiasaph. The generations are not flattened or every similarly named occurrence merged. The Numbers survival notice does not name each son.

Phinehas' later priesthood episode and Eleazar's later Levite leadership are linked through explicit parentage, without supplying Putiel's daughter's personal name. No modern permission for violence is derived from the priesthood episode.

The Aaron/Moses genealogy headings are compared with the commission they frame. The summary saying they brought Israel out is not used to claim that the first Pharaoh audience already accomplished the actual departure.

Without eloquence, weak of voice and slow of tongue remain the supplied speech descriptions. No uncircumcised-lips phrase or medical diagnosis is substituted. The god-to-Pharaoh/prophet wording in7:1 remains distinct from matters-pertaining-to-God and mouth-to-the-people wording in4:16.

God's explicit future hardening, later narrator attribution to God, grew-strong/grew-hard notices without a named agent, God's heavy-heart assessment, and Pharaoh's later making his own heart heavy are kept distinct. Romans is a later theological discussion, not claimed to quote7:3 or to resolve every agency formulation.

The eighty/eighty-three age notice is retained as supplied, including its singular speaking wording. Stephen's forty-plus-forty recollection and Aaron's123-year death notice are comparisons of stated markers, not a newly reconstructed chronology of every intervening event.

Moses' private serpent-staff scene is distinguished from Aaron's public dragon-staff scene. The source reports the enchanters' transformations, Aaron's staff swallowing their staffs, and their later failure with gnats; no replacement creature term or independent explanation of sorcery is imposed.

The pinned2 Timothy passage names Jannes and Jambres opposing Moses. It is retained as a later allusion to opposition, without adding those names to Exodus or claiming independently resolved identities for every wise man, sorcerer or enchanter.

Exodus7:17 gives God's I-strike declaration;7:19 commands Moses to instruct Aaron;7:20 names both brothers and then uses a singular he;7:25 attributes the strike to the Lord. The unresolved singular is not independently assigned and these narrative levels are not collapsed.

The source's wood-and-stone blood wording is not replaced by a newly supplied vessel or idol interpretation. The earlier water-poured-on-dry-ground verification and the later Egypt-wide waters judgment retain their different scale and setting.

Fish deaths, stench, inability to drink and digging are linked to the stated warnings, without claiming the digging succeeds. The psalm's rain-waters and singular frog expressions remain its own wording and do not add new events or a frog census to Exodus.

Seven days passing after the river strike is not turned into an explicit statement that the blood condition ended after exactly seven days. The frog household-invasion and removal location lists remain distinct; Moses' promised removal words to Pharaoh are not quoted as the unreported words of his later prayer.

editorial_notes.note: This edition has28 source units in chapter8. Its frog warning is7:26-29 and the actual bringing-up begins8:1-2; conventional32-verse chapter8 numbering was not substituted. Aaron's staff action, Moses' intercession and the Lord's response remain distinct. The enchanters' reported imitation is not newly explained as either illusion or an independently tested mechanism.

Tomorrow, the river exception, frog deaths, heaps and stench retain their supplied scopes. Gnats are not silently replaced with lice. The enchanters' finger-of-God confession is their statement; Luke11:20 is a later distinctive-expression comparison, not a claim that gnats are demons or that Luke explicitly quotes these speakers.

Dog-flies, Goshen, people-and-livestock distinctions and Israelite light are retained for their particular plagues. The comparison of exemptions does not invent an unreported blanket protection from every Egyptian affliction. Promised release, actual refusal and the prayed-for relief are kept as different actions.

In-land sacrifice, not going far, men-only permission, household permission without livestock and Moses' full-party demand remain different stated proposals. Moses' forecast of stoning is not a recorded stoning or a new identification of Egyptian sacred species. Lord-be-with-you and evil-lies-before-you remain Pharaoh's own words without a supplied narrator's conversion or motive verdict. You shall also give us offerings is not reduced to an independently documented transfer arrangement.

Became-heavy, passive-hardened, Pharaoh-made-heavy and Lord-hardened formulations retain their respective speakers and agency.9:12 ends as the Lord had commanded;9:35 has the Lord's earlier speech to Moses. Neither human nor divine formulations are erased by the later Romans interpretation, and no complete causal system is independently asserted.

Livestock in the plains in the warning, all Egyptian livestock in the death notice, protected Israelite livestock and later references to animals are all preserved. No import, repopulation or hidden survivor roster is invented. Four-footed animals, furnace soot and blistering boils retain their actual terms; neither a modern disease diagnosis nor a new anatomical location for every case is inferred from Deuteronomy's later Egyptian-ulcer comparison.

The knowledge/power/name purpose is stated in the speeches.9:15 uses future I will stretch out and strike, not an imported could-have counterfactual.9:16's preserved and Romans9:17's raised-you-up forms remain distinct within the explicit later scriptural quotation. Unprecedented-hail statements retain their created-Egypt and nation-origin comparison wording, without a new climate record or creation date.

Some attendants heed the warning and shelter livestock; others leave it exposed. These actions do not independently determine every attendant's conversion status or resolve Moses' later general assessment of fear. Hail, fire, thunder and rain remain their actual narrated elements. Flax/barley damage and late wheat/spelt survival qualify broad crop damage; no additional harvest month or weather mechanism is assigned. Pharaoh's confession is distinguished from subsequent narrated sin/refusal.

The Lord's statement that He hardened hearts and mocked the Egyptians is preserved alongside the command to recount signs to children and grandchildren. The later household-teaching passages are linked to the specific Exodus memory rather than a new universal claim about an ethnic population.

The south wind brings the locusts, and a strong wind from the sea removes them into the Red Sea; east/west and Sea-of-Reeds substitutions are not made. Hand-over-land command and staff-toward-heaven performance retain their distinct words. The land is described as ruined after vegetation is eaten, not silently darkened by locusts. Later Psalm larvae and crop terms remain in that later passage. This death is Pharaoh's description of the crisis, not his reported death.

Darkness that may be felt, gloom, tempest, three days and no one rising from bed remain as supplied. Wisdom's roof/prison/workplace imagery and contrasting holy light are labelled later theological reflections, not additional eyewitness details inserted into Exodus. The face ban, reply and later summons are compared without inventing a physical audience or declaring the later summons an independently proven broken promise.

The exact Saints70 target records and Greek/Septuagint Psalm numbering were used. Later poems, prayers and theological interpretation retain their different plant, animal, agency and spatial descriptions. Wisdom of Solomon remains a Saints70 book; no extra canon book or replacement edition was introduced.

editorial_notes.note: Retain one further plague, secretly spoken request instructions, lending, and Moses' standing before Egyptians, Pharaoh and attendants. Do not use favour to invent Pharaoh's completed repentance. The midnight entrance and firstborn warning remain the Lord's words within Moses' speech. Servants' predicted bowing is not separately narrated in the departure account and is not declared independently witnessed.

The earlier female slave beside the mill and later captive woman in the pit remain distinct supplied descriptions, alongside the firstborn livestock. The great-cry and dog-growling expressions are not converted into independently verified demographic or zoological studies. Earlier Goshen dog-flies and livestock protections are labelled distinct prior judgments, not the same event.

Keep the first-month framework, tenth-day household selection, fourteenth-day slaughter toward evening, evening-to-evening unleavened bounds and first/seventh assemblies. The later first-month/fifteenth-day calendar expressions and delayed second-month observance retain their actual conditions. No modern date, hour calculation or independent calendrical harmonization is claimed.

Household sheep, neighbour sharing, counted portions, male year-old unblemished animals from lambs/young goats, fire roasting and whole-animal details remain intact. The source already includes no-bone-breaking at12:10 as well as12:46. Deuteronomy's boil-and-roast wording remains alongside Exodus's exclusion of boiling in water; the parallel identifies actual related Passover instructions rather than a new lexical solution.

Peter's Christ-lamb imagery is labelled later redemption imagery, not an exact quotation of every Passover specification. Luke expressly frames Jesus' meal as Passover; its bread/cup interpretation and remembrance command are later uses with their own commemorated event, not substituted details of the Egyptian meal. Paul explicitly applies Passover and unleavened imagery to Christ and the community. John explicitly cites Scripture about the unbroken bone, but no exclusive identification of its only Old Testament background is claimed; Psalm 33:21 was also read.

Preserve doorway blood, hyssop, blood beside the door and the no-exit rule; no basin wording is inserted. The Lord announces and performs the Egyptian judgment, sees the blood and does not permit the destroyer into the protected houses. The Lord and destroyer are not independently collapsed into one identified figure or replaced with an unquoted angel designation. Hebrews' faith interpretation and blood-sprinkling account remain a later summary with its own agency wording.

Girded loins, sandals, staffs, haste and the night vigil retain their specific forms. Dough and kneaded batches in garments are not silently changed into a different object list. Moses' prospective family-explanation instruction uses remembered deliverance language; it is not used to relocate the later narrated judgment earlier. The child-question parallels distinguish Passover, firstborn redemption and general-law teaching contexts.

The narrator attributes the firstborn judgment to the Lord, the release order to Pharaoh and expulsion pressure to Egyptians. Do not invent an individually narrated blessing of Pharaoh after his request. The livestock permission reverses the earlier restriction; the mixed multitude is not assigned a new exhaustive ethnic roster or universal responsibility for later complaints. Gifts retain favour, lending and plundering wording without modern legal adjudication.

Preserve about 600,000 footmen apart from the household company, distinct from the later 603,550 military enrolment with its age criterion. Keep Rameses-to-Succoth and the station list's stated departure date. The 430 years concern residence in both Egypt and Canaan in this source; Paul's covenant-to-law 430 and Genesis's foreign-affliction 400 are compared without equating all chronological scopes or silently removing Canaan.

The foreigner, household slave, purchased slave, sojourner, hired worker and resident-foreigner categories retain their supplied labels. Circumcision of every male belonging to the Passover-seeking resident foreigner and subsequent participation as a native remain explicit. No new lexical theory collapses every status, no universal exemption is invented, and one-law parity is not used to erase the stated eligibility requirements. No modern civil-policy recommendation or approval of slavery is inferred.

The repeated obedience notices explicitly name Moses and Aaron. The departure summaries retain the host and day wording; no additional same-day phrase or independent timetable is inserted. Later Sinai observance is distinguished from the first Egyptian instruction.

Every retained target belongs to Saints70 and has actual pinned readable evidence. Revelation remains in that canon; no Revelation passage was read or retained here and the existing missing-pinned-record candidate gap is not declared resolved.

peer_review_receipts.review_outcome: Approved. No required rationale corrections, pair removals, source-identity errors or missing same-chapter labels found.
confirmed_distinctions: The source chapter boundary is preserved: the frog threat is in7:27-29, and Aaron's instruction and outbreak begin8:1-2. No common-edition renumbering is substituted.

The commanded and performed frog/gnat actions preserve Aaron as actor. The enchanters' reported frog success, later failure with gnats and later physical incapacity from boils are distinguished without a new explanation of sorcery.

The Tomorrow appointment, the Lord's acting as Moses said, deaths in inhabited settings and the separate river-frog exception remain distinct. The gathering and stench are not made an independently diagnosed medical event.
Gnats and dog-flies retain the supplied creature terms; no lice substitution, new species identification or new chronology from the psalm's grouping is introduced.

The enchanters' finger-of-God statement and Luke11:20's use of that expression are compared as distinct contexts. The Luke reference is not labelled an explicit Exodus quotation and does not equate demons with gnats.
Pharaoh's requests for prayer and promises of release remain speech. Subsequent refusals are not treated as fulfilled permission or the earlier confessions as proof of lasting conversion.

The Goshen, livestock and firstborn distinctions are each tied to their own warnings or narrated results; they are not made a blanket assertion that every earlier plague left every Israelite unaffected.

Moses' objection to sacrifice before Egyptians preserves the feared stoning as his stated reason, not a narrated stoning. The object of the abomination and the Egyptian cult are not independently reconstructed.
The livestock warning retains in-the-plains wording and the outcome retains all. Later livestock in the hail warning is not supplied with an invented replacement-herd or imported-survivor account.
The Egyptian-ulcer comparison in Deuteronomy is a later Egypt-linked affliction reference, not a modern diagnosis or a claim that every curse detail is narrated in the Exodus plague.

The I-will-strike death statement in9:15 remains future wording rather than a substituted could-have-struck conditional. The preserved wording of9:16 remains beside Romans' raised-you-up wording, explicitly distinguished within the later scriptural use.

The extraordinary-hail comparisons retain the warning's created-Egypt wording and narrator's nation-origin wording. No new historical weather date or independently verified meteorological maximum is claimed.

The shelter warning, attendants gathering livestock and others leaving them exposed remain distinct responses. No roster of sheltered people, death count or universal statement about every attendant's belief is invented.

The broad vegetation damage is read with the explicit flax/barley versus wheat/spelt qualification. Later locust consumption concerns hail-spared vegetation without a new list of every survivor or a fixed harvest month.

The psalms' hail/fire and named plants remain their own poetic descriptions. Wisdom16:16-19 is attributed as later theological reflection on the extraordinary fire-and-water combination rather than an independent scientific mechanism.

God's sending thunder and hail, Moses' stretched hand and prayer, and the stated lists of ceased elements are distinguished. The later cessation notice is not made a separately enumerated repetition of every earlier fire/thunder/rain item.

Moses' statement that Pharaoh and attendants have not yet feared the Lord remains his spoken assessment and does not erase the narrator's earlier attendant who feared the word and sheltered livestock.

Explicit divine hardening, Pharaoh's making hearts heavy, passive hardening notices and agency-unspecified became-heavy clauses retain their different wording and attribution. Romans is a later theological interpretation, not a new resolution of every agency expression.

The command to transmit the signs to descendants is compared with later household teaching that expressly recounts Egyptian slavery, signs and deliverance; the links are particular to that narrative memory.

The attendants' destruction warning, Pharaoh's party-size question, men-only restriction and later household-but-no-livestock offer remain separate speech stages. His Lord-be-with-you wording is not made the narrator's statement of conversion.

The locust arrival retains the Lord's south wind and raised staff, beside the command's hand-over-land wording. Removal retains the strong wind from the sea and Red Sea destination; no east/west replacement is imposed.
The narrative's before-and-after unprecedented-locust claim and the psalm's innumerable larvae remain supplied forms without a modern population maximum or an added larval stage in Exodus.
Pharaoh's request to remove this death is his description of the affliction, not a report that Pharaoh is already dead. No unquoted prayer formula is inserted.

The source darkness includes gloom, a tempest, three days and inability to rise from bed; Israel has light everywhere it lives. These details remain beside Wisdom's later roofs, farmers, shepherds, wilderness workers and figurative imprisonment rather than being silently merged.

Wisdom18:1 supplies an explicit contrast of light for holy ones and others unable to see their forms, supporting the later light/darkness reflection without importing every Wisdom episode into the Exodus narrator.

The psalm's provoked-His-words clause is not assigned a newly chosen antecedent. Moses' demand that Pharaoh give offerings remains its supplied wording, not an unreported provision arrangement; the later livestock departure is not claimed to list each offering Pharaoh furnished.

The threatened face-to-face ban, Moses' response and later summons remain distinct statements. The links do not invent another court visit, an execution, or an independently resolved physical arrangement for every later scene.

Etham, Bouthan, settlement, Eiroth, Migdol and Baal-zephon forms remain visible; no independent site equivalence or modern border map is asserted. Cloud/fire guidance and continued accompaniment are grounded in the actual passages. The angel-of-God and pillar movements retain their stated agency and positions. Poetic wind language is not used to overwrite the south direction, and no independent claim about Pharaoh's personal death is made beyond the stated entering force.

Paul's baptism-into-Moses interpretation and Hebrews' faith/crossing interpretation are expressly later theological readings of the identified cloud/sea event. They are not inserted as a literal baptism ritual in Exodus, nor made into an unsupported assertion that every later member remained faithful.

The narrated rescue and belief correspond to the Psalm's rescue, belief and praise sequence. The Psalm's following forgetfulness was also read; no permanent-perfect-faith conclusion is added to the initial response. Moses remains the supplied attendant rather than an independently elevated divine identity.

Each retained rationale names a specific legal, memorial, narrative, quoted or explicitly interpretive connection. Intrachapter links concern repeated formulas, commands and outcomes, particular actors, locations, physical actions or narrated transitions. No link requires removal for unread evidence or a forced specific allusion.
